title: feat(service-datasource): a code-defined datasource reads its credential from OS_DATASOURCE_<NAME>_PASSWORD
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBR9NEQPF4XiEBhFuE3M9hKB)_

Fixes #27687

Clause-②: yes (widening) — `@objectstack/service-datasource` exports `datasourceEnvCredentialVar`, `resolveDatasourceEnvCredentialsSwitch`, `DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS_SWITCH` and the `DatasourceEnvCredentialSource` type, and `DatasourceConnectionServiceConfig` gains the optional `envCredentials`; `@objectstack/spec/data` exports `CODE_DEFINED_CREDENTIAL_ROUTE`. Nothing an author writes is added or refused, and no existing key changes meaning.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

1. 代码里声明的数据源（`defineDatasource` / 包内 `*.datasource.ts`）现在在连接时读 `OS_DATASOURCE_<名字>_PASSWORD`，例如 `warehouse` → `OS_DATASOURCE_WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD`。
2. 只在主机开关 `OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS=on` 时读；`os serve` / `os start` / `os dev` 默认开，其他组合（云端、多租户、自建 kernel）默认关；其他取值启动即拒绝。
3. 只读代码数据源（按来源集合判定，从不看记录的 `origin`）；UI/API 创建的同名数据源、`default` 都不读。
4. 声明了 `credentialsRef` 或 `connector` 时它们优先，失败仍然 fail-closed，不回落到环境变量；变量没设时，失败原因会写出该设哪个变量；值不进日志、不进任何应答。
5. 信任后果：`os serve` 下本地安装的包也读这个槽，所以任何已安装的包都能声明任意空闲名字的数据源，从而读到对应变量。文档和 changeset 已写明。
6. 规范层只改了拒绝文本（5 条凭据拒绝 + 2 条 `password` 提示共用一句新句子），accept 集合不变；changeset 全部 `patch`（`Metadata-protocol: none` 时门禁要求 patch，见下文）。

## The ruling

Maintainer ruling on #27687 (option 5, recorded by the seat in comment 6525963988, claim amended in 6525977981): a datasource defined in code reads its credential at connect time from a runtime environment variable whose name the platform derives from the datasource name. The seat's follow-ups: the switch is opt-in in `os serve` / `os start` with the library default off and no tenancy coupling, the off value is spelled `off`, and the install-local route (#28132) keeps reading the slot, with its trust consequence stated and pinned.

## Measurements on `origin/main` `d70e94ae`

**(a) The seam where the CLI host turns the switch on.** No new public option was needed. `os serve` loads `@objectstack/service-datasource` dynamically and builds `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` itself (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, the `adminMod` block). The plugin's `init()` reads `process.env`, so `serve` stamps `OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS=on` into its own environment just before it builds the plugin, when the operator left it unset or empty. That is the same seam `os start` uses for `OS_CRYPTO_AUTOKEY` (`start.ts:482`). `os start` spawns `serve` (`start.ts:528`) and `os dev` spawns `serve --dev` (`dev.ts:848`), so both inherit the stamp. Every other composition never runs that line and stays off.

**(b) The shape of `secret`.** `DatasourceConnectionSpec.secret?: string` (`contracts/datasource-driver-factory.ts`) is the cleartext the connection service hands to `factory.create`. Its readers in `default-datasource-driver-factory.ts`: postgres puts it in `password` (`:603`, `:611`), mysql the same (`:830`, `:839`), mongodb puts it in the `MongoClient` `auth` block (`:945`, `:1047`), and turso reads it ahead of `config.authToken`. sqlite, sqlite-wasm and memory have no credential slot. The slot fills exactly this value, so it reaches every built-in driver that takes a secret. A plugin driver that resolves its credential per request (OData, through `DATASOURCE_SECRET_RESOLVER_SERVICE`) does not read it; the docs say so.

**(c) Where `CODE_DATASOURCE_NAMES_SERVICE` is filled, and how `connect()` gets it.** Three producers, all in `@objectstack/runtime`, all through `contributeCodeDatasourceNames` (`code-datasource-names.ts:156`):
- `app-plugin.ts:626`: the boot artifact's declared datasources;
- `default-datasource-plugin.ts:150`: `default`;
- `declared-datasources.ts:160`: a package installed into the running kernel (install-local, since #28132).

`connect()` gets it as a callback. The admin plugin passes `isCodeDatasource(name)`, which reads the set through `codeDatasourceNamesOf(ctx)`, the same reader `servedOrigin` uses. The set is read at each connect, never cached at `init()`, so a name an install adds later is honoured.

## What changes

- **`DatasourceConnectionService.connect()`**, after the `credentialsRef` and connector steps: when neither is declared, the connect is not `asDefault`, the slot is configured (switch on), the trigger is `declared-auto`, and the name is in the code set, it reads `OS_DATASOURCE_<NAME>_PASSWORD`. `<NAME>` is the name upper-cased with each non-`[A-Z0-9]` character replaced by `_`. A non-empty value becomes the build's `secret`.
- **`resolveDatasourceEnvCredentialsSwitch()`**: unset or empty is off; `on` / `off` in any letter case; anything else throws `OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS must be 'on' or 'off', got '<value>'. …`. The admin plugin calls it in `init()`, so the boot is refused.
- **`os serve`** stamps the `on` default (`packages/cli/src/utils/datasource-env-credentials-default.ts`).
- **`planCredentialMigration`**'s code-origin remedy names the row's variable and the switch.
- **Spec prescriptions**: one shared sentence, `CODE_DEFINED_CREDENTIAL_ROUTE`, appended to the credential refusals and the two `password` guidance entries (before/after below).
- **Docs**:
  - `external-datasources.mdx` §4 gains "A datasource defined in code: the environment variable". It covers the derivation table, an example, the switch and its default, the code-only rule, precedence, the unset case, collisions, the plugin-driver limit, and a warning callout on who can read the variable (installed packages; why the switch is off on multi-tenant hosts).
  - `drivers.mdx`: the Multi-Datasource paragraph and the read-only sample now teach the variable instead of a `sys_secret:` handle a code author cannot mint.

### Deviations from the order, stated

- **Unset variable: the verdict stays `failed-degraded`, not `failed-credentials`.** The order says "keep the existing `failed-credentials` verdict", but the existing verdict for a code datasource connecting with no password is the driver's own connect failure, `failed-degraded`, so keeping it means `failed-degraded`. Only the reason changes: it gains "— datasource '<name>' is defined in code and reads its credential from `OS_DATASOURCE_<NAME>_PASSWORD` at connect, which is not set on this host". If the database accepts the connection without a password, nothing changes. A bound datasource still refuses the boot, and the thrown message names the variable.
- **Collision refused at connect, not "at boot" as a separate pass.** Datasource names must match `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`, so two names that pass the schema can never derive one variable. The guard is defensive: the second connect is refused as `failed-credentials` with both names and the variable, and its variable is never read. On the boot path that refusal is a boot failure whenever the datasource is fail-fast.
- **Five refusals carry the sentence, not four**: `INLINE_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED`, `URL_EMBEDDED_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED`, `URL_CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAM_REFUSED`, `PASSTHROUGH_INLINE_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED`, and `PASSTHROUGH_NESTED_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED`. The fifth prescribes the same "bind it instead" route and would otherwise send a code author to the same unfollowable door. The `.describe()` on `refusedInlineCredentialKey` carries it too, which is why four generated driver reference pages moved.
- **Changeset levels are `patch` on all three packages, not minor.** The seat asked for service-datasource minor and cli minor, but `check-changeset-no-major` refuses a `minor` beside `Metadata-protocol: none` ("`none` -> every introduced entry `patch`"). `none` is the measured kind: no key, value or metadata type an author writes changes.

## Before / after for each string

The shared sentence (`CODE_DEFINED_CREDENTIAL_ROUTE`, in `packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts`):

> A datasource defined in code (`defineDatasource`) leaves the credential out of the declaration: it is read at connect time from the runtime environment variable derived from the datasource name (`OS_DATASOURCE_WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD` for a datasource named `warehouse`), which `os serve` / `os start` honour by default (`OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS=on`).

Each string below is unchanged up to its last sentence. The after-text is the before-text plus ` ` + the sentence above.

| String | Before ends with | After |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `INLINE_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED` | "…always wins over anything embedded in `config`." | + the sentence |
| `URL_EMBEDDED_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED` | "…do not pass through this publish door and are unaffected." | + the sentence |
| `URL_CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAM_REFUSED` | "…do not pass through this publish door and are unaffected." | + the sentence |
| `PASSTHROUGH_INLINE_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED` | "…a `${…}` span anywhere in `options` is itself refused at publish." | + the sentence |
| `PASSTHROUGH_NESTED_CREDENTIAL_REFUSED` | "…a `${…}` span anywhere in `options` is itself refused at publish." | + the sentence |
| `refusedInlineCredentialKey` `.describe()` | "…never stored in `config`." | + the sentence |
| `ExternalDatasourceSettingsSchema` guidance `password` | "…it never dereferences a hand-written path." | + the sentence |
| `DatasourceSchema` guidance `password` | "…a managed datasource included." | + the sentence |

Every one keeps the Setup → Datasources and `external.credentialsRef` routes, and none carries a `#NNNN`; the test below checks both. `planCredentialMigration` code-origin remedy:
- **Before:** "Move the credential in the source that defines this datasource: bind it through `external.credentialsRef`, or supply it from the runtime environment."
- **After:** "Move the credential out of the source that defines this datasource: leave it out of the declaration and set `OS_DATASOURCE_<NAME>_PASSWORD` in the runtime environment, which the datasource reads at connect when the host's `OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS` switch is on (the default under `os serve` / `os start`), or bind it through `external.credentialsRef`." The real row's variable is substituted.

## Guards and their tests (each ablated)

Unit pins are in `packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/datasource-env-credential.test.ts` (24 tests). Kernel wiring is in `packages/runtime/src/datasource-env-credential.test.ts` (3, a real admin plugin and the real driver factory). The CLI pins are in `packages/cli/src/utils/datasource-env-credentials-default.test.ts` (4) and the spec pins in `packages/spec/src/data/driver/code-defined-credential-route.test.ts` (16). Every ablation used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` against the committed tree and restored to `blob == HEAD`.

| Guard | Test | Ablation → red |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A code datasource connects with the variable set | "a code datasource connects with the variable set", "through `connectDeclared`", runtime "switch on: the boot artifact's datasource…" | A8 (switch resolver returns off) → 13 red; A10 (admin wiring `isCodeDatasource` → false, rebuilt dist) → runtime 1 red |
| Install-local reads the slot (trust consequence) | "a name the host registers after construction (an install-local package)", runtime `connectPackageDatasources(…, installed: true)` | A10 → runtime red |
| `registerPool` / runtime-admin never reads it | "the same name created through the admin door…" | A2 (drop the `declared-auto` check) → 2 red |
| Provenance, never `origin` | "a caller-set `origin: 'code'` is not provenance" | A3 (drop `isCodeDatasource`) → 1 red |
| Switch off: no read | "a host that did not opt in", runtime "switch unset" | A10 (runtime); unit: no-slot case reads nothing |
| Switch refuses other values | "refuses %j…" ×5, runtime "a value other than `on` / `off` refuses the boot" | A8 → 5 red |
| A declared `credentialsRef` wins and stays fail-closed | "a resolving `credentialsRef` is the secret", "an unresolvable `credentialsRef`… does NOT fall back" | A4 (drop `!credentialsRef`) → 1 red |
| `default` keeps `OS_DATABASE_URL` | "an `asDefault` connect never reads the slot" | A11 (drop `!opts.asDefault`) → 1 red |
| Unset variable: the reason names it | "the database refusing the login answers the variable to set", "an EMPTY variable is unset" | A6 (drop the reason suffix) → 2 red |
| Collision refused | "the second name is refused with both names and the variable" | A5 (disable the owner check) → 1 red |
| The value in no log line or answer | "no log line, connect answer or connection state carries it" | A7 (log the value) → 1 red |
| Every rewritten refusal parses its own example back | spec `describe.each` over 7 refusal families: the example name is read out of the message, the credential is left out of the very artefact that was refused, and the result parses with no secret in it | A1 (drop the sentence from the nested refusal) → 2 red; A12 (example variable drifts to `OS_DATASOURCE_WH_PASSWORD`) → 1 red |
| The example is the variable the runtime derives | service "is the variable the spec refusals' worked example names" (`datasourceEnvCredentialVar(name) === variable`, and the switch name matches) | reads spec through `dist`; pinned against the rebuilt dist |
| `os serve` stamps before the plugin is built | cli "stamps once…", "the stamp precedes the plugin construction" | A9 (remove the stamp) → 2 red |

That stays true for a database."
